transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-03-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Park (OptiForge VP Eng), Marco Ruiz (OptiForge SRE), Anika Shah (OptiForge Head ML Ops), Tom Becker (OptiForge CFO)

Summary: Quick QBR-style checkin focused on recent peg-like latency spikes, cost variability in peak windows, capacity options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), and roadmap alignment for an upcoming retail feature rollout. Customer wants clearer cost predictability and to validate fallbacks for degraded capacity.

Topics: usage patterns, spike mitigation, caching/quantization levers, security/compliance ask, pricing scenarios, pilot next steps

Action items (see metadata)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everybody thanks for joining. Quick roll call, you all good?
[00:12] Lena Park: Yup hi Jordan, hi Priya. We had a quick internal - sorry - just coming from a standup.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Hey, hello. Quick agenda: status, then dive into the latency spike on Friday, then cost scenarios and dedicated sizing.
[00:30] Tom Becker: Sounds good, budget angle front and center for us.
[00:37] Marco Ruiz: I'll flag SRE notes, we did some short blips around 11pm PST on Friday.
[00:45] Jordan Ellis: Ok great. First, high-level numbers: your token spend was up 42% week over week, cost per 1M tokens drifted because of longer average sequence lengths during peak sale windows. That ties to the timeouts you saw.
[01:05] Anika Shah: Right — we ran longer context in sessions, more product history. We anticipated some bump but not that amplitude.
[01:12] Marco Ruiz: The spike behavior looked like a small number of long-request tails causing worker saturation, KV cache thrash maybe. We saw more cache misses under the new prompt set.
[01:32] Priya Nair: That matches what we instrumented: when the prefix isn't cached, latency climbs nonlinearly due to repeated KV lookups and larger attention windows. There's also batching interplay — our default batch policy tried to pack several long seqs and that increased tail latency.
[01:55] Lena Park: So question: is that an infra issue or model? Is Redwood Dedicated going to help or do we need Private/VPC?
[02:12] Jordan Ellis: Good Q. Short answer: Dedicated will get you predictable throughput and isolated GPU pools which reduces noisy neighbor effects and gives better tail latency. Private/VPC gives network isolation and customer-managed keys but is heavier ops and licensing. Hosted can still work if we tune batching, cache TTLs, and use quantized variants for some routes.
[02:45] Tom Becker: cost comparison? Because Dedicated is a fixed commit, while Hosted is variable.
[02:52] Jordan Ellis: We'll put numbers in a sheet but rough: Dedicated commit could lower per-token unit cost by ~20-35% for steady high throughput but you pay the reserved capacity commitment. Hosted is pay-as-you-go—higher unit but no commit.
[03:12] Tom Becker: Can you show a blended scenario where peak windows are bursty? We don't want to overcommit.
[03:20] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We often recommend a hybrid: Dedicated baseline for predictable traffic and Hosted burst to absorb spikes. There's an automatic routing policy that can route by latency or cost.
[03:38] Marco Ruiz: Any gating on model variants when falling back? We're concerned about semantic degradation if it routes to a smaller quantized model.
[03:48] Priya Nair: Yes you can pin model versions per route. Fallbacks can be set to specific variants and we can enable quality-preserving quantization profiles. We also support canary rollouts to test perceived quality.
[04:12] Anika Shah: How are you measuring 'perceived quality'? We need to tie regressions to eval sets, not just log perplexity.
[04:22] Jordan Ellis: Agreed — Redwood Optimize ties quality regressions to prompt sets and will alert on drift in metrics you choose. We can onboard your retail prompt set and run the eval harness.
[04:36] Lena Park: Ok let's talk security — Tom wants to ensure auditability and encryption in transit AND at rest. We also need SSO for dev teams.
[04:44] Tom Becker: SOC 2 and ISO, plus SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integration for key rotations.
[04:52] Priya Nair: We support SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC at the token and route level, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private. For Hosted, we surface customer key management options; for Dedicated we can lock keys to the pool. We'll share the SOC 2 pack and network diagrams after.
[05:10] Marco Ruiz: How are logs/audit events retained? We need 180 days for compliance.
[05:16] Jordan Ellis: Audit logs retention is configurable at enterprise tiers. We can enable 180-day retention and export to your SIEM.
[05:25] Marco Ruiz: Great. On the technical deep-dive: we want Priya or another SE to see how batching policy interacts with our request patterns — for example, 300ms versus 50ms latency SLOs.
[05:36] Priya Nair: Sure — we should run a 48-hour load test with your sample traffic so we can tune batching thresholds and prefix cache TTLs.
[05:46] Lena Park: We'll provide a representative traffic dump — Marco will send that.
[05:51] Marco Ruiz: Yup I'll drop a sanitized 2-week sample by Monday.
[05:58] Jordan Ellis: Perfect. Let's talk quantization and model recommendations quickly — you're currently on an open Llama-style variant, right?
[06:07] Anika Shah: Yes, a fine-tuned LLM with some proprietary ranking.
[06:12] Priya Nair: We can profile it: sometimes going from FP16 to an 8-bit quantized runtime reduces cost significantly with minimal quality hit if done with the right calibration. We'll propose quantization profiles per workload.
[06:28] Anika Shah: Are there tooling/CI hooks for regression testing after quantize?
[06:33] Jordan Ellis: Yes — Redwood Optimize can run regression evals against your golden prompts and block a rollout if quality drops below thresholds.
[06:42] Tom Becker: Back to money — what's the expected ROI timeline if we go Dedicated + burst?
[06:49] Jordan Ellis: If your peak hours are a small fraction we might not fully amortize a large commit. But with a modest Dedicated baseline sized to 60-70% of steady usage and Hosted burst, you typically see payback in 3-6 months depending on seasonality. We'll model it.
[07:10] Marco Ruiz: On SLA side: what are the uptime SLAs and latency SLOs for Dedicated?
[07:16] Priya Nair: Dedicated gets an SLA for uptime (we'll provide the legal) plus latency targets per model tier. We'll include tail latency numbers per model/instance type in the performance profile.
[07:30] Lena Park: Anything about multi-region failover? We need cross-region fallback during major cloud outages.
[07:37] Jordan Ellis: Yes, Smart routing can route by region and price/latency. For cross-region failover we recommend geo-redundant Dedicated pools or Hosted fallback pairs. We'll outline a warm/cold strategy.
[07:50] Marco Ruiz: Ok good. One more: caching — you mentioned prefix caching and KV. Are there best practices for e-comm flows where session history grows?
[07:59] Priya Nair: For long session histories we recommend aggressive prefix compaction and TTLs; store user state externally and pass condensed context to the model. Also use per-customer cache keys to avoid cross-tenant thrash. We have a runbook on this.
[08:18] Anika Shah: We'll want that runbook plus a short workshop.
[08:23] Jordan Ellis: We'll do both. Next steps recap coming up.
[08:30] Lena Park: Any competitors we should be aware of? We've had procurement ask about Anthropic pricing and a few infra vendors like Run:ai.
[08:38] Jordan Ellis: Noted. From a feature perspective our differentiator is model-quality-preserving fallbacks plus unified tooling across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. We'll highlight that in the deck.
[08:50] Tom Becker: Ok. Final questions?
[08:55] Marco Ruiz: No more from SRE, I think timeline and test plan are key.
[08:59] Priya Nair: We'll schedule the 90-min technical deep-dive with Marco and Anika; aim for week of 3/29.
[09:08] Jordan Ellis: Great. I'll send pricing scenarios by end of day Wednesday (3/22) and Priya will share the KV/prefix cache whitepaper. Marco will give us sample traffic. We'll also spin up a 48-hour load test once we have the data.
[09:24] Lena Park: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[09:28] Tom Becker: Thanks.
[09:32] Jordan Ellis: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the sheets.

End of transcript.
